text:
elaine: Heads-up — ran a 12h sampling of the continuous-batcher on a mixed tenant mix (60% short, 40% long). Seeing recurring short-tenant starvation during 99th pct spikes.
raj: Interesting, can you paste the perf sketch? numbers?
elaine: TL;DR: short-req p99 latency +60ms vs baseline, throughput flat. KV hit-rate for short seqs drops ~18% during congested windows.
sam: do we have kernel-selection mismatches? i.e. long sequences forcing slower kernels that block short fastpath?
elaine: yes. profiler shows a 40% increase in fastpath eviction when a long batch wins the slot. snippet: ```
# top call sites (samples)
serve_loop_kernel_fastpath 48.2%
serve_loop_kernel_general 31.5%
kv_warmup_lock 8.9%
batch_coalesce 7.4%
```
sasha: hmm could be batch formation bias: current batcher prefers fill-factor over tenant fairness — it greedily waits to reach target tokens. long requests inflate target and delay short ones.
raj: Proposed quick experiments: (A) token_budget_cap per-batch (hard cap) so long queries can't expand batch beyond X tokens, (B) short-priority lane that gets a minimum credit slice every N ms, (C) early-eject for batches with >Y% long tokens. Which one to try first?
elaine: did A+B in sandbox overnight. Results: A reduced p99 short latency by ~42ms, but overall tokens/sec fell 3%. B kept throughput, reduced short p99 by 58ms and improved KV hit-rate for short seqs by ~9%.
sam: can you share the config we used?
elaine: ```
batcher.token_cap = 5120   # global per-batch token cap
batcher.short_lane_min_credit_ms = 8
batcher.early_eject_threshold = 0.6
```
raj: Nice. Any regressions for long tenants?
elaine: long p95 increased ~18ms in A, negligible in B. But we saw one regression: when KV warmup is slow, short requests still miss because the KV priming costs a slot. perf-bot: automated trace attached: https://perf.example/reports/3097654321
sasha: So we need KV warmup overlap with batching — maybe allow speculative KV fetch for pending short requests while waiting for batch formation? Might be tricky with memory.
sam: Another idea: broker credits between tenants: if a tenant has >Z% of running tokens, throttle their batch expansion and allocate spare credits to short-tenant queue. Essentially a dynamic slice broker.
elaine: ran a micro-probe for slice-broker with threshold=0.55. It rebalanced well but added scheduling jitter. Telemetry: unfairness index (Gini) dropped from 0.27 -> 0.12, short p99 improved 64ms. jitter increased median scheduling latency by 4ms.
raj: Those tradeoffs look ok. Ops: need to add canary with perf regression guard for long-tenants p95 +50ms. Also add KV warmup metric to alert.
sasha: Can we add kernel-hinting based on composition? If batch contains >70% short sequences prefer fastpath kernel; else fallback. Might reduce kernel churn.
sam: Agree, but we must ensure kernel-selection switch time is cheap. Elaine, can you run traces for kernel-change overhead?
elaine: scheduled. Initial trace shows kernel swap cost ~1.6ms cold, 0.4ms hot. With our p99 targets it's acceptable.
nash: @dev-bot can you spin a canary with short-lane min-credit=8ms and slice-broker threshold=0.55 for 2 hours on us-west-2? tag: rv-ctch-05
dev-bot: @elaine canary started: rv-ctch-05 on us-west-2, cohort=5% traffic. Logs: /canary/rv-ctch-05
raj: Good. Next: add experiment to validate eviction ordering — prefer evict oldest long-kv entries first to reduce impact on short sequences.
sasha: Also add telemetry: per-tenant kv-warmup-latency histogram, batch-composition ratio, and a short-starve counter.
elaine: I'll open a tiny RFC with configs + canary dashboards. quick notes in case we lose thread: 1) short-priority lane is winner for fairness 2) token-cap to avoid runaway batch growth 3) slice-broker to smooth longer-term imbalance 4) KV warmup overlap remains unresolved but mitigated by small kernel hinting.
sam: ack, thanks.
raj: +1. if canary looks good we'll ship to prod with rollback guard. :thumbsup:
elaine: will follow up with the RFC link and perf graphs when canary finishes.
